claims.text: less effective than other oral drugs, and often stopped for GI effects.
claims.quote: Alpha-glucosidase inhibitors are less effective than other oral medications in reducing plasma glucose, and patients often stop the medications because they may cause dyspepsia, flatulence, and diarrhea.

claims.text: Can be combined with all other oral drugs and with insulin.
claims.quote: can be used in combination with all other oral antihyperglycemic medications and with insulin

claims.text: Acarbose 25 mg PO TID with the first bite of each main meal;
claims.quote: The recommended starting dosage of acarbose is 25 mg given orally three times daily at the start (with the first bite) of each main meal.

claims.text: max 50 mg TID if ≤60 kg, 100 mg TID if >60 kg.
claims.quote: The maximum recommended dose for patients ≤ 60 kg is 50 mg t.i.d. The maximum recommended dose for patients > 60 kg is 100 mg t.i.d.
Acarbose Tablets are contraindicated in patients with diabetic ketoacidosis or cirrhosis.

claims.text: IBD, colonic ulceration, partial or predisposition to intestinal obstruction.
claims.quote: Acarbose Tablets are also contraindicated in patients with inflammatory bowel disease, colonic ulceration, partial intestinal obstruction or in patients predisposed to intestinal obstruction.

claims.text: Charcoal and carbohydrate-splitting digestive enzymes (amylase, pancreatin) reduce its effect; don't take together.
claims.quote: Intestinal adsorbents (for example, charcoal) and digestive enzyme preparations containing carbohydrate-splitting enzymes (for example, amylase, pancreatin) may reduce the effect of acarbose and should not be taken concomitantly.

claims.text: Changes digoxin bioavailability (digoxin dose may need adjusting).
claims.quote: Acarbose has been shown to change the bioavailability of digoxin when they are coadministered, which may require digoxin dose adjustment.

claims.text: Adds to hypoglycemia risk with a sulfonylurea or insulin.
claims.quote: Because acarbose given in combination with a sulfonylurea or insulin will cause a further lowering of blood glucose, it may increase the potential for hypoglycemia.

claims.text: Check transaminases every 3 months in the first year, then periodically.
claims.quote: It is recommended that serum transaminase levels be checked every 3 months during the first year of treatment with acarbose and periodically thereafter.

claims.text: Treat hypoglycemia (when on a sulfonylurea or insulin) with oral glucose (dextrose), not sucrose.
claims.quote: Oral glucose (dextrose), whose absorption is not inhibited by acarbose, should be used instead of sucrose (cane sugar) in the treatment of mild to moderate hypoglycemia.

claims.text: Overdose doesn't cause hypoglycemia; it causes transient flatulence, diarrhea and abdominal discomfort.
claims.quote: Unlike sulfonylureas or insulin, an overdose of acarbose will not result in hypoglycemia. An overdose may result in transient increases in flatulence, diarrhea, and abdominal discomfort which shortly subside.

claims.text: No carbohydrate drinks or meals for 4–6 h.
claims.quote: In cases of overdosage the patient should not be given drinks or meals containing carbohydrates (polysaccharides, oligosaccharides and disaccharides) for the next 4 to 6 hours.
